text:
mike-ops: Heads up — noticed a strange variance on the Feb marketplace invoices. AWS shows a -$42,300 adjustment under 'Marketplace credits' that doesn't match our reserved capacity offsets. @anya-finance can you take a first pass?

anya-finance: Yep saw that too when pulling the monthly close. Summary: expected committed credits = $320,000, invoice reported credits = $277,700. Delta = $42,300. No obvious refund memo in the portal.

sophia-eng: Do we have SKU-level mapping for reserved pools -> marketplace SKUs? Sometimes the marketplace line items don't map 1:1 with our internal pool names.

mike-ops: We do, but mapping's messy for cross-region failover pools. Posting a quick extract of the lines that look odd: 

```
invoice_line_item_id, sku, region, marketplace_credit, internal_commit_credit
li-9876, compute.gpu.p4d, us-west1, 15000, 30000
li-9877, compute.gpu.v100, us-east1, -4200, 0
li-9880, commit-commitment-adjust, global, -42300, -42300
```

dan-cloud: That `compute.gpu.v100` negative looks like an adjustment for a refund we processed last month tied to a cancellation. But the big -42300 global line is weird — could be a reconciliation offset applied by vendor for prior overstated credits. Need the marketplace statement PDF + invoice JSON.

anya-finance: I pulled the marketplace statements from both AWS and GCP for Feb and combined them. Attaching the filenames in S3: s3://billing-archive/2026/02/aws_marketplace_statement_feb.pdf and s3://billing-archive/2026/02/gcp_marketplace_statement_feb.pdf (link in original thread).

billing-bot: Automated note: invoice LI tags updated for 1769723456 in billing-queue. Please attach root-cause and GL impact within 48h.

olivia-pm: From product side — this could affect committed capacity forecasting for Dedicated customers if those credits are being under-applied. We need to confirm whether this is purely a billing artifact or a true credit reversal.

sophia-eng: Suggestion: run a quick query joining our internal reservations table to the raw invoice line items to find mismatches. Example BigQuery pseudocode: 

```sql
SELECT r.pool_id, i.sku, SUM(i.marketplace_credit) as invoice_credit, SUM(r.expected_commit_credit) as expected_credit
FROM `redwood.billing.invoice_lines` i
LEFT JOIN `redwood.ops.reservations` r ON i.sku = r.marketplace_sku AND i.region = r.region
WHERE i.invoice_date BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28'
GROUP BY r.pool_id, i.sku
HAVING ABS(SUM(i.marketplace_credit) - SUM(r.expected_commit_credit)) > 1000
```

mike-ops: I've kicked off that query and will paste results in ~15m. For now, @anya-finance can you check whether the vendor applied any global reconciliation adjustments in previous months? Look for credit memos with ids like `recon-*` or `adjust-*`.

anya-finance: On it. Also checking contract terms: some marketplace vendors net prior over-allocations against current month which would explain the one-line global negative. If that's the case, we need to reflect it in the revenue accounting and update forecast.

dan-cloud: Quick note — there was a cluster migration in us-west1 on Feb 10 where we moved several Dedicated pools to a new pool id. If invoices reference old pool ids, automatic joins will miss them. I'll provide a mapping file: 

```
old_pool_id,new_pool_id,marketplace_sku
pool-33,pool-97,compute.gpu.p4d
pool-44,pool-98,compute.gpu.v100
```

mike-ops: Results from the join query (snippet): 

```
pool-97, compute.gpu.p4d, invoice_credit=15000, expected_credit=30000
pool-98, compute.gpu.v100, invoice_credit=-4200, expected_credit=0
pool-unmapped, commit-commitment-adjust, invoice_credit=-42300, expected_credit=-42300
```

mike-ops: So the -42300 matches an internal expected reversal (we marked a cancellation), but the p4d 15k vs 30k mismatch persists — looks like only half the committed credit was applied.

anya-finance: I'll open a ticket with AWS Marketplace support and attach the mapping + invoice JSON. Can someone from eng confirm the pool->sku mapping and supply the commit contract IDs?

sophia-eng: I'll pull the commit contract IDs and the commit start/end dates. Expecting: commit-ct-2025-09 for pool-97 covering Sep25-Feb26.

olivia-pm: Action items: 1) anya to escalate to AWS Marketplace support with attached join results and mapping. 2) sophia to supply commit contract IDs and migration mapping. 3) dan to verify cluster migration metadata so joins are accurate. 4) mike to update billing-queue with interim GL flags.

mike-ops: Adding to billing-queue now and marking interim impact as P&L risk up to $42.3k.

anya-finance: Opening support case — case id AWS-CASE-112233. I'll paste updates here. If support confirms a vendor-side reversal that shouldn't have applied to our account, we'll request a corrected invoice or credit memo.

billing-bot: Reminder: please include invoice_line_item_id and invoice_json when filing the support case.

sophia-eng: Provided commit ids in the case comments and attached the migration mapping. Also flagged that pool-97 had a billing alias in the marketplace: `redwood-dedicated-us-west1-p4d` — might be how AWS split the credit.

anya-finance: Support responded: initial response says the global adjustment is an upstream reconciliation from partner; they are investigating the p4d partial application. They asked for a ledger-level trace for li-9876.

mike-ops: I'll export the ledger trace for li-9876 and upload to the case.

olivia-pm: Let's reconvene tomorrow after support replies. If this is recurring (same pattern in Jan/Dec), we should escalate account team.

mike-ops: Thanks all. I'll post the ledger file when done and update last_message_ts once we have support resolution. :thumbsup:
